variableReadSpelling: VARIABLE-READ SPELLING (php, 2026-10-11). The `uses` targets in this file that name a `$variable` are BINDINGS, not declaration names: the analyzer spells a variable read as `<read source>\u0000<binding>` with `metadata.localBinding`, because a local/param/superglobal is never a published symbol and the BARE name let the store bind the read to an unrelated same-named declaration in another file. The defect and its counterfactual are in validation/m14/fixtures/php/local-read-phantom.mts; the whole-population effect is in docs/analyzers/history/php-lane-notes.md. What each row PINS (which read, from where, and how many) did not move.
rationale: R10 (#835) — the dynamic-callee spelling contract. A `calls` target is the name of a CALLEE; `$callable()` names nothing, because the callee is a runtime VALUE. The pre-R10 rule took the callee node's raw text, so the lane published `calls -> $callable` (measured in phpmyadmin's tests: `calls -> $controller` in LicenseControllerTest.php:23) — again IDENTICALLY on both sides, because the oracle's truth came from the same shape. A probe over 400 real php files (phpunit/src, phpmyadmin/src + tests) found 1,047 `name` callees and `variable_name` the ONLY non-name shape reaching the rule (1 site), so this narrows a fabrication rather than a capability. What the call EVALUATES is still read, and that read is the variable pass's `uses` edge — the fix adds the honest edge's owner and removes the fabricated name in the same move, which is why the fixture requires both halves: `uses -> handler` MUST be present and `calls -> handler` MUST be absent, while a named callee in the same method (`$this->run(...)`) still emits its `calls` edge.
